critic raised a concrete objection: The blend is unit-inconsistent: you add a “seasonal_trend” of 11.6115 directly to quarterly EPS in USD/share. A $11.6115 per-share quarterly component is implausible versus ADI’s FY2026Q3 guidance of $3.30 ± $0.15 (range $3.15–$3.45) and likely represents either an annual EPS figure or an 11.6115% rate. This wrong-scale input inflates the result to 3.5115, even pushing it above the guided top end ($3.45). The seasonal term must be converted to a quarterly USD/share basis (or applied as a percentage to the base), not added as $11.6115.
Adjusted gross margin: critic raised a concrete objection: You’ve double-counted FY2025Q3. For a FY2026Q3 forecast, the “last 4 reported” quarters are FY2026Q2, FY2026Q1, FY2025Q4, and FY2025Q3—so taking the mean of those four (70.85%) and then averaging it again with the prior-year same period FY2025Q3 (69.2%) gives FY2025Q3 five times the weight of any other quarter. That methodological error drags your base from 70.85% down to 70.025% before the +0.400 pp tilt, biasing the final 70.425% figure.
